tasks.spec:
You are an INDEPENDENT AUDITOR. Another AI agent spent a long session changing a video podcast pipeline and made a list of specific factual claims about what it did. The owner does not want to take those claims on trust. Your job is to RE-RUN each claim and report what you actually observe.

You must NOT modify, create, or delete any file except ./audit.md in your own current working directory. Do not run git commands that write: no commit, checkout, stash, reset, push, merge, or branch. Read-only git is fine: log, show, diff, status, grep. Do not call any MCP tool or App. Do not capture anything to an external system. Set PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 on any python you run so you do not litter the repo.

THE REPOSITORY IS AT /mnt/d_drive/repos/podcast. The episode under test is at /mnt/d_drive/repos/podcast/episodes/2026-06-10-fred-cho. Read them; do not write to them.

HOW YOU ARE GRADED. Your report must contain a line for every claim in the form `CLAIM-NN: VERDICT` where VERDICT is exactly PASS, FAIL, or UNVERIFIABLE, and each must be followed by the exact command you ran and what it printed. A verdict with no command is rejected. Agreeing with the other agent is not the goal; being right is. If a claim is overstated, partially true, or true only under conditions the claimer did not state, say so and mark it FAIL or UNVERIFIABLE rather than being generous.

BE ADVERSARIAL. Assume the claims are inflated until your own commands say otherwise. Where a claim is technically true but misleading, say that explicitly in your notes even if you mark it PASS. Look especially for: numbers that do not reproduce, tests that pass for a reason other than the one claimed, guards that exist but are never called, and work described as finished that is actually behind a default-off flag.

THE CLAIMS, verify each independently:

CLAIM-01: The full test suite currently reports 2044 passed and exactly 1 failed, and that single failure is an environment-variable test unrelated to media. Run the suite yourself: `cd /mnt/d_drive/repos/podcast && PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 python3 -m pytest tests/ -q -p no:cacheprovider --ignore=tests/test_media_gates.py`. Report the real numbers and name the failing test.

CLAIM-02: Five commits exist on branch feat/one-true-master implementing this work, and nothing has been pushed to any remote. Check `git log --oneline`, and check whether the branch has an upstream and whether it is ahead of it.

CLAIM-03: The rendered composite at /mnt/d_drive/repos/podcast/episodes/2026-06-10-fred-cho/processed/composite_GRID.mp4 certifies against the stems at 12 of 12 probe points with 0.0ms drift. Run the certifier yourself: `cd /mnt/d_drive/repos/podcast/episodes/2026-06-10-fred-cho/processed && python3 /mnt/d_drive/repos/loop-factory/ringer/one-true-master/checks/certify_episode.py --stems stems --target composite_GRID.mp4 --points 12 --tolerance-ms 40`. Report the actual worst drift and how many probes certified. Also inspect that script and say whether its PASS condition is meaningful or whether it could pass trivially.

CLAIM-04: The certifier genuinely discriminates, meaning it FAILS a bad render. Run the same certifier against /mnt/d_drive/repos/podcast/episodes/2026-06-10-fred-cho/processed/composite_FIXED.mp4, which is claimed to be off by a constant 225.0ms. Report whether it fails and what drift it reports.

CLAIM-05: The transcript at /mnt/d_drive/repos/podcast/episodes/2026-06-10-fred-cho/processed/transcript.json now lands on the session grid. Specifically: the host track's last segment ends at about 2840.0s against a session length of 2842.196s, and ZERO host segments start inside the host audio dropout window. The dropout is in /mnt/d_drive/repos/podcast/episodes/2026-06-10-fred-cho/processed/timeline.json. Compute this yourself from the two JSON files and report the real numbers.

CLAIM-06: av_sync.verify_sync and media_gates.validate_raw_tracks were previously dead code, never called in production, and are now actually called from server/pipeline/orchestrator.py. Grep the repo and report where each is called from. Distinguish production call sites from tests and standalone scripts.

CLAIM-07: The stem content pin halts the pipeline on BOTH a mismatched pin and a MISSING pin, and a missing pin is not treated as a pass. Find verify_stem_content_pin in server/pipeline/av_sync.py, find where the orchestrator consumes its result, and report what actually happens in each of the three cases the function can return.

CLAIM-08: PTS divergence enforcement is ON for grid-aligned stems and OFF for raw tracks, deliberately, because a raw track that lost packets has large divergence by construction. Check the default in media_gates.validate_raw_source_integrity and check what the orchestrator passes for stems versus raw.

CLAIM-09: A camera-dropout auto-switch rule exists at a 5-second threshold, is a named constant rather than a magic number, and is actually wired into the render path rather than merely defined. Find the constant and every place it is used.

CLAIM-10: composite_side_by_side refuses to accept per-track offsets when called in stems mode, so the historical double-shift bug is structurally impossible rather than merely avoided by convention. Find the guard and prove it by calling the function in stems mode with offsets and observing the error, without rendering anything.

CLAIM-11: tests/test_orchestrator_transcription_contract.py catches a real bug rather than being decorative. It is claimed to fail if the fix in server/pipeline/orchestrator.py is reverted. Verify by reading the test and the call site it inspects, and reason about whether reverting would fail it. Do NOT actually revert the file; you are read-only. If you cannot verify without writing, mark it UNVERIFIABLE and say what you would need.

CLAIM-12: The work is additive and the raw, non-grid path still exists and still functions, so this did not silently remove the old behavior. Check whether the grid paths are behind flags or defaults, and whether the raw path is still reachable.

OUTPUT: write ./audit.md. Open with a two-sentence bottom line: is the overall picture the other agent painted accurate, overstated, or wrong. Then one section per claim, numbered CLAIM-01 through CLAIM-12, each with its verdict line, the command you ran, the real output, and a note if the claim is technically true but misleading. Close with a section listing anything you found that the other agent did NOT claim and should have disclosed.
